faq.q: Why does naming a feeling help?
faq.a: When you put a feeling into words, the thinking part of your brain switches on and the alarm part calms down. So the feeling gets a little smaller and easier to handle.
asks: What does name it to tame it mean?
Does saying my feeling out loud help?

faq.q: Is it bad to feel angry?
faq.a: No. Anger is a normal feeling that tells you something seems unfair. What matters is what you do with it: you can say it with words instead of hurting anyone.
asks: Am I bad if I get angry?

faq.a: Yes, it is okay to cry. Crying is a natural way your body lets out big feelings, and many people feel calmer afterwards. Boys and girls, children and grown-ups all cry.
asks: Why do I cry when I am sad?

faq.q: What if I do not know what I am feeling?
faq.a: That is very normal. Notice your body, like a tight tummy or a hot face, and look at a feelings chart. You can also tell a grown-up you trust "I feel funny inside" and work it out together.
asks: I feel weird but I do not know why

faq.q: Can I feel two feelings at once?
faq.a: Yes! You can feel excited and nervous before a trip, or happy and sad when a holiday ends. Mixed feelings are completely normal.
asks: Can you be happy and sad at the same time?

facts: A 2007 brain-scan study at the University of California, Los Angeles found that putting a feeling into words calmed the brain's alarm area, the amygdala.
Psychologist Paul Ekman found that faces showing happiness, sadness, anger, fear, surprise and disgust are recognised by people in many cultures around the world.
